diagnosis: The supplied raw archive is empty; two current development cases and one accepted-candidate aggregate are available. Their six actual execution_result events comprise five successes and one timeout: the salon has two successful builds followed by a failed third attempt; the compartment has three successful builds. Both first builds succeeded with the API safeguards, although no earlier raw baseline establishes causality. The salon's final correction received only about 79.7 seconds for execution after generation and produced no required output; its intended apron, placement and tone fixes therefore remain unvalidated. Its selected scene contains 1,864 meshes and 379,401 vertices, versus 235 meshes and 6,576 vertices for the compartment. This supports investigating construction cost, without attributing all elapsed time to mesh count. The salon still shows an overly open tubular apron, rigid pillow, excessive subject extent and a lighter floor; the compartment retains recognizable major objects but differs in berth/locker coverage, foreground cropping, occlusions and broad illumination. Each case's three completed regression renders are separate from reconstruction counts. Material and move operations passed on Architecture and berths respectively, certifying those prescribed operations only. The +10% focal interventions held geometry fixed and lowered overall scores by approximately 0.001162 and 0.003163 for salon and compartment; individual metrics were mixed. These global camera interventions do not test the named regression groups' scale, establish an optimal lens or identify true geometry. Selection completion and functional aggregates support retaining the working safeguards, but provide no evidence that this proposed change improves quality.
rationale: Test whether economical first builds and measured time reserves preserve successful construction while enabling useful visual correction. The policy now budgets complete execute wall time, rechecks time after generation, and requests selection when another revision is unlikely to finish. Instructions explain SceneAct's primitive expansion and prioritize filled silhouettes and narrow, evidence-supported changes. Expected evidence is lower construction time on expensive cases, fewer timeout attempts, preserved first-build validity and edit passes, and improved completed outputs—not merely fewer meshes or fewer attempts. No evaluation or rendering was performed here.
interpretation: Intervention sensitivity and later shared-code outcome are shown separately. This is not proof that the probe caused a gain; other development cases and terminal results remain necessary.
